pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: 
  closes #22630 <!-- REMOVE this line if no issue to close -->

Problem Summary:

Original sliding window algorithm is not efficient enough(`O(logN) inserte/delete, O(N) space`), improve it with deque to get amortized `O(1) insertion/deletion` and `O(windowSize)` of space.

### What is changed and how it works?

Proposal: #22630 
What's Changed: 

- Implemented Deque-based sliding window algorithm
- Added a `windowInfo` struct inside all `maxMinXXXSliding` struct to store absolute index of each window
- Added a `MaxMinSlidingWindowAggFunc` interface to support `maxMinXXXSliding` in window init and `PartialResult` reset


How it Works:

Improved original sliding window from `heap` + `map` method to Deque-based.

Benchmark:

issue_context.title: Improve max/min sliding window function algorithm with deque
issue_context.body:
## Development Task

### Current status
 
Currently TiDB is using a `heap` + `map` based sliding window algorithm, where for each element in the heap we also store how many time it was inserted. Then when we query what the smallest/biggest element is, we discard it if its index is zero. Problem with this `late deletion` technique is performance deteriorates badly when input gets larger, since `heap` and `map` keep on increasing their sizes.

### How to improve

A better solution would be using a deque-based version. The trick to this is to store the numbers in a deque and whenever inserting a number x we remove all numbers at the back of the deque which are greater than equal to x. The front of the queue might have a value which shouldn't be in the window anymore, but we can use the lazy delete idea with the deques as well. Now each element of window is inserted into the deque and deleted from the deque at most once. 


### Performance improvement

Time Complexity improvement: O(logN)  ------> Amortized O(1) insert/delete
Space Complexity:  O(N) ------> O(W), W for window size

### Other benefits:

A deque-based sliding window should also be easier to add external storage function(#14392) as well.

review_comments: Deque needs the absolute position of each element, here `i` only denotes the relative position in `rowsInGroup`. To get the absolute position, we need to add offset of `e.start`, which represents the absolute index of start of window.
The `maxMin4XXXSliding` still implements `SlidingWindowAggFunc` interface,  the code can run to here?

Yes, code could run to here. 

In this PR, `maxMin4XXXSliding` implements 3 interfaces:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/34013484/106736856-f17f4a00-6650-11eb-88c8-fc89450d7497.png)

We still need `SlidingWindowAggFunc` for `Slide` method to run sliding window function. But in deque-based algo, I need the absolute index of window start, but directly changing `UpdatePartialResult()` signature is cubersome, so I came up with a compromise solution, setting window start index inside a `windowInfo` which is composited with all `maxMin4XXXSliding` struct. 

In order to distinguish `maxMin4XXXSliding` from other `aggFuncs`, I implemented `MaxMinSlidingWindowAggFunc` for them. Therefore during window initialization(window.go:L339-L449), all `maxMin4XXXSliding` could be picked up by asserting type of `MaxMinSlidingWindowAggFunc` and pass in window related info.
Thanks for your explanation, I already understand your solution.
